questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Define a relation $R$ on the interval $\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$ by $x R y$ if and only if $\sec^2 x - \tan^2 y = 1$. Then $R$ is:
options: both reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive
both reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
questions.solution:
$x R y : \sec^2 x - \tan^2 y = 1$
Check reflexive:
$x R x = \sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1$, $\forall x \in \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$
Check symmetric:
$x R y \Rightarrow y R x$
$\sec^2 x - \tan^2 y = 1$
$= \sec^2 y - \tan^2 x = (1 + \tan^2 y) - (\sec^2 x - 1)$
$= 2 - (\sec^2 x - \tan^2 y)$
$= 2 - 1 = 1$
$\Rightarrow y R x$
Check transitive:
$x R y$ and $y R z$
$\Rightarrow \sec^2 x - \tan^2 y = 1$
$\sec^2 y - \tan^2 z = 1$
Add $\Rightarrow \sec^2 x - \tan^2 z + (\sec^2 y - \tan^2 y) = 2$
$\Rightarrow \sec^2 x - \tan^2 z + 1 = 2 \Rightarrow x R z$
$\Rightarrow R$ is an equivalence relation.

questions.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle formed by the lines $7x - 6y + 3 = 0$, $x + 2y - 31 = 0$ and $9x - 2y - 19 = 0$. Let the point $(h, k)$ be the image of the centroid of $\Delta ABC$ in the line $3x + 6y - 53 = 0$. Then $h^2 + k^2 + hk$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Points of intersections are $(9, 11)$, $(3, 4)$, $(5, 13)$
Centroid of $\Delta ABC = \left(\frac{17}{3}, \frac{28}{3}\right)$
Since during image of $\Delta ABC$ about line will reflect the whole triangle including centroid, reflected centroid will be image of $\left(\frac{17}{3}, \frac{28}{3}\right)$ about $2x + 6y - 53 = 0$
$\frac{x - \frac{17}{3}}{2} = \frac{y - \frac{28}{3}}{6} = \frac{-2\left(2\left(\frac{17}{3}\right) + 6\left(\frac{28}{3}\right) - 53\right)}{2^2 + 6^2}$
$\Rightarrow h = 3, k = 4$
$\Rightarrow h^2 + k^2 + hk = (h + k)^2 - hk$
$= 49 - 12 = 37$

questions.text: Let $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = 3\hat{i} - 5\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}$ be a vector such that $\vec{a} \times \vec{c} = \vec{c} \times \vec{b}$ and $(\vec{a} + \vec{c}) \cdot (\vec{b} + \vec{c}) = 168$. Then the maximum value of $|\vec{c}|^2$ is
questions.solution:
$\vec{a} \times \vec{c} = \vec{c} \times \vec{b} = -(\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$
$\Rightarrow (\vec{a} \times \vec{c} + \vec{b} \times \vec{c}) = (\vec{a} + \vec{b}) \times \vec{c} = 0$
$\Rightarrow \vec{c}$ is parallel to $\vec{a} + \vec{b}$.
$\vec{c} = \lambda(5\hat{i} + (-6)\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}) \Rightarrow |\vec{c}|^2 = \lambda^2(77)$
$(\vec{a} + \vec{c}) \cdot (\vec{b} + \vec{c}) = \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + |\vec{c}|^2 + \vec{c} \cdot (\vec{a} + \vec{b})$
$= (6 + 5 + 3) + |\vec{c}|^2 + \lambda(25 + 36 + 16) = 168$
$\Rightarrow |\vec{c}|^2 + \lambda(77) = 154$
$\Rightarrow 77\lambda^2 + 77\lambda - 152 = 0$
$\Rightarrow \lambda^2 + \lambda - 2 = 0$
$\Rightarrow (\lambda + 2)(\lambda - 1) = 0$
$|\vec{c}|^2_{\text{max}} = (-2)^2(77) = 308$

questions.text: Let $y = y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\cos x (\log_e (\cos x))^2 dy + (\sin x - 3y \sin x \log_e (\cos x)) dx = 0$, $x \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$. If $y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{-1}{\log_e 2}$, then $y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$\frac{dy}{dx} - \frac{3 \sin x}{\cos x \ln \cos x} y = -\frac{\sin x}{\cos x (\ln \cos x)^2}$
I.F. $= e^{-\int \frac{3 \tan x}{\ln \cos x} dx}$
Let $\ln \cos x = t$
$-\tan x dx = dt$
e^{\int \frac{3 dt}{t}} = e^{3 \ln t} = t^3 = (\ln \cos x)^3
Solution will be
$y(\ln \cos x)^3 = -\int (\tan x)(\ln \cos x) dx$
$y(\ln \cos x)^3 = \frac{(\ln \cos x)^2}{2} + c$
$\because y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = -\frac{1}{\ln 2}$
$\Rightarrow c = 0$
$\therefore y = \frac{1}{2(\ln \cos x)}$
$y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{\ln \cos \frac{\pi}{6}}$
$= \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{\ln \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}$
$= \frac{1}{2 \ln \sqrt{3} - \ln 2} = \frac{1}{\ln 3 - \ln 4}$

questions.text: The integral $80 \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \frac{\sin\theta + \cos\theta}{9 + 16\sin 2\theta} d\theta$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4} \frac{\sin\theta + \cos\theta}{9 - 16\sin 2\theta} d\theta$
Take $\sin\theta - \cos\theta = t$
$(\cos\theta + \sin\theta)d\theta = dt$
$(\sin\theta - \cos\theta)^2 = t^2 \Rightarrow \sin 2\theta = 1 - t^2$
$\theta = 0 \rightarrow t = -1$
$\theta = \frac{\pi}{4} \rightarrow t = 0$
$I = \int_{-1}^{0} \frac{dt}{9 + 16(1 - t^2)} = \frac{1}{16} \int_{-1}^{0} \frac{dt}{\frac{25}{16} - t^2}$
$= \frac{1}{4} \left[ \frac{1}{10} \log \left| \frac{5+4t}{5-4t} \right| \right]_{-1}^{0} = \frac{1}{40} [0 + \log_e 9] = \frac{\log_e 9}{40}$
$80 I = 2 \log_e 9 = 4 \log_e 3$

questions.text: Let the area of the region \{(x, y) : 2y \le x^2 + 3, y + |x| \le 3, y \ge |x - 1|\} be $A$. Then $6A$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$A = \int_{-1}^{1} \left( \frac{x^2+3}{2} + (x-1) \right) dx + \int_{1}^{2} ((3-x) - (x-1)) dx$
$\Rightarrow \left[ \frac{x^3}{6} + \frac{3x}{2} + \frac{x^2}{2} - x \right]_{-1}^{1} + \left[ 3x - \frac{x^2}{2} - \frac{x^2}{2} + x \right]_{1}^{2}$
$A = \frac{7}{3} \Rightarrow 6A = 14$

questions.text: Let $L_1 : \frac{x-1}{1} = \frac{y-2}{-1} = \frac{z-1}{2}$ and $L_2 : \frac{x+1}{-1} = \frac{y-2}{2} = \frac{z}{1}$ be two lines. Let $L_3$ be a line passing through the point $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$ and be perpendicular to both $L_1$ and $L_2$. If $L_3$ intersects $L_1$, then $|5\alpha - 11\beta - 8\gamma|$ equals
questions.solution:
$L_3 : \frac{x-\alpha}{a} = \frac{y-\beta}{b} = \frac{z-\gamma}{c}$
$(a\hat{i} + b\hat{j} + c\hat{k}) \parallel (\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) \times (-\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k})$
$(a, b, c) = (5, 3, -1)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{x-\alpha}{5} = \frac{y-\beta}{3} = \frac{z-\gamma}{-1} = \lambda$
Point of intersection:
$\alpha = p + 1 - 5\lambda, \beta = -p + 2 - 3\lambda, \gamma = 2p + 1 + \lambda$
$\Rightarrow |5\alpha - 11\beta - 8\gamma| = 25$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Let $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{10}$ be ten observations such that $\sum_{i=1}^{10} (x_i - 2) = 30$, $\sum_{i=1}^{10} (x_i - \beta)^2 = 98$, $\beta > 2$, and their variance is $\frac{4}{5}$. If $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$ are respectively the mean and the variance of $2(x_1 - 1) + 4\beta, 2(x_2 - 1) + 4\beta, \dots, 2(x_{10} - 1) + 4\beta$, then $\frac{\beta\mu}{\sigma^2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\sum_{i=1}^{10} (x_i - 2) = 30 \Rightarrow \sum x_i = 50 \Rightarrow \text{Mean} = 5$
\text{Variance} = $\frac{4}{5} = \frac{\sum x_i^2}{10} - (\bar{x})^2 \Rightarrow \sum x_i^2 = 258$
Now, $\sum_{i=1}^{10} (x_i - \beta)^2 = 98 \Rightarrow 258 - 2\beta(50) + 10\beta^2 = 98 \Rightarrow \beta^2 - 10\beta + 16 = 0 \Rightarrow \beta = 8$ as $\beta > 2$
New observations: $2x_1 + 30, 2x_2 + 30, \dots, 2x_{10} + 30$
$\mu = 2(5) + 30 = 40$
$\sigma^2 = 2^2 \left(\frac{4}{5}\right) = \frac{16}{5}$
$\frac{\beta\mu}{\sigma^2} = \frac{8 \times 40}{\frac{16}{5}} = 100$

questions.solution:
$T_{k+1} = {}^{n}C_k 7^{\frac{n-k}{3}} 11^{\frac{k}{12}}$
12 divides $k$ and 3 divides $n - k$.
Multiples of 12 for $k$ would work.
$k = 0, 12, 24, \dots$
$k_{\max} = 12 \times 182 = 2184$
Minimum value of $n$ will be 2184.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The number of solutions of the equation $\left(\frac{9}{x} - \frac{9}{\sqrt{x}} + 2\right)\left(\frac{2}{x} - \frac{7}{\sqrt{x}} + 3\right) = 0$ is
questions.solution:
Let $\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} = t$
$(9t^2 - 9t + 2)(2t^2 - 7t + 3) = 0$
$9t^2 - 9t + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow t = \frac{2}{3}, \frac{1}{3}$
$2t^2 - 7t + 3 = 0 \Rightarrow t = \frac{1}{2}, 3$
$\sqrt{x} = \frac{3}{2}, 3, 2, \frac{1}{3} \Rightarrow x = \frac{9}{4}, 9, 4, \frac{1}{9}$
Hence, number of solutions = 4

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Consider an A.P. of positive integers, whose sum of the first three terms is $54$ and the sum of the first twenty terms lies between $1600$ and $1800$. Then its $11^{\text{th}}$ term is:
questions.solution:
Let A.P. be $a, a + d, a + 2d$
$3a + 3d = 54 \Rightarrow a + d = 18 \quad \dots(1)$
$1600 < \frac{20}{2}[2a + 19d] < 1800$
$160 < 2a + 19d < 180$
$160 < 18 \times 2 + 17d < 180$
$\frac{124}{17} < d < \frac{144}{17}$
Since $d \in \text{integer} \Rightarrow d = 8$
$a + d = 18 \Rightarrow a = 10$
$a_{11} = a + 10d = 10 + 10 \times 8 = 90$

questions.text: Let the ellipse $E_1 : \frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$, $a > b$ and $E_2 : \frac{x^2}{A^2} + \frac{y^2}{B^2} = 1$, $A < B$ have same eccentricity $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$. Let the product of their lengths of latus rectums be $\frac{32}{\sqrt{3}}$, and the distance between the foci of $E_1$ be $4$. If $E_1$ and $E_2$ meet at $A, B, C$ and $D$, then the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ equals
questions.solution:
$2ae = 4 \Rightarrow a = 2\sqrt{3}$
$1 - \frac{b^2}{12} = \frac{1}{3} \Rightarrow b^2 = 8$
$\frac{2b^2}{a} \times \frac{2A^2}{B} = \frac{32}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow A^2 = 2B$
$1 - \frac{A^2}{B^2} = \frac{1}{3} \Rightarrow B = 3 \Rightarrow A^2 = 6$
Solving $E_1: \frac{x^2}{12} + \frac{y^2}{8} = 1$ and $E_2: \frac{x^2}{6} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1$ gives vertices of rectangle:
$(x, y) = \left(\pm \frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{5}}, \pm \frac{6}{\sqrt{5}}\right)$
$\text{Area} = \frac{24\sqrt{6}}{5}$

questions.text: Let $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$. Let $L_1 : \vec{r} = (-\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}) + \lambda \vec{a}, \lambda \in \mathbf{R}$ and $L_2 : \vec{r} = (\hat{j} + \hat{k}) + \mu \vec{b}, \mu \in \mathbf{R}$ be two lines. If the line $L_3$ passes through the point of intersection of $L_1$ and $L_2$ and is parallel to $\vec{a} + \vec{b}$, then $L_3$ passes through the point
questions.solution:
$\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$
$\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$
$L_1 : \vec{r} = (-\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}) + \lambda \vec{a}, \lambda \in \mathbf{R}$
and $L_2 : \vec{r} = (\hat{j} + \hat{k}) + \mu \vec{b}, \mu \in \mathbf{R}$
$\vec{a} + \vec{b} = 3\hat{i} + 9\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$
$L_1 : \vec{r} = (\lambda - 1)\hat{i} + 2(\lambda + 1)\hat{j} + (\lambda + 1)\hat{k}$
$L_2 : \vec{r} = 2\mu \hat{i} + (7\mu + 1)\hat{j} + (1 + 3\mu)\hat{k}$
For point of intersection of $L_1$ & $L_2$
$\lambda - 1 = 2\mu$ and $2(\lambda + 1) = 7\mu + 1$
$\Rightarrow \lambda = 3$ and $\mu = 1$
$L_3 : \vec{r} = 2\hat{i} + 8\hat{j} + 4\hat{k} + \alpha(3\hat{i} + 9\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$
For $\alpha = 2$
$\vec{r} = 8\hat{i} + 26\hat{j} + 12\hat{k}$

questions.text: Two parabolas have the same focus $(4, 3)$ and their directrices are the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis, respectively. If these parabolas intersects at the points $A$ and $B$, then $(AB)^2$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
The parabolas are
$(x - 4)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = x^2$ ...(i)
and $(x - 4)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = y^2$ ...(ii)
If point of intersection are $A(x_1, y_1)$ and $B(x_2, y_2)$
By solving (i) and (ii), we get
$x_1 + x_2 = 14$ and $x_1 x_2 = 25$
$(AB)^2 = 2((x_1 + x_2)^2 - 4 x_1 x_2) = 192$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Let the line $x + y = 1$ meet the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 4$ at the points $A$ and $B$. If the line perpendicular to $AB$ and passing through the mid-point of the chord $AB$ intersects the circle at $C$ and $D$, then the area of the quadrilateral $ADBC$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Solving $x = y$ & $x^2 + y^2 = 4$ gives
$C(\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2})$ and $D(-\sqrt{2}, -\sqrt{2})$
Solving $x + y = 1$ & $x^2 + y^2 = 4$ gives
$A\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{7}}{2}, \frac{1-\sqrt{7}}{2}\right)$ & $B\left(\frac{1-\sqrt{7}}{2}, \frac{1+\sqrt{7}}{2}\right)$
Required area $= 2 \times \frac{1}{2} \begin{vmatrix} \sqrt{2} & \sqrt{2} & 1 \\ \frac{1-\sqrt{7}}{2} & \frac{1+\sqrt{7}}{2} & 1 \\ -\sqrt{2} & -\sqrt{2} & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 2\sqrt{14}$ sq. units

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Let $[t]$ be the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then the least value of $p \in \mathbf{N}$ for which
$$\lim_{x \to 0^+} \left( x \left( \left[\frac{1}{x}\right] + \left[\frac{2}{x}\right] + \dots + \left[\frac{p}{x}\right] \right) - x^2 \left( \left[\frac{1}{x^2}\right] + \left[\frac{2^2}{x^2}\right] + \dots + \left[\frac{9^2}{x^2}\right] \right) \right) \ge 1$$
is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
$\lim_{x \to 0^+} \left( x \left( \left[\frac{1}{x}\right] + \left[\frac{2}{x}\right] + \dots + \left[\frac{p}{x}\right] \right) - x^2 \left( \left[\frac{1}{x^2}\right] + \left[\frac{2^2}{x^2}\right] + \dots + \left[\frac{9^2}{x^2}\right] \right) \right) \ge 1$
$\Rightarrow (1 + 2 + 3 + \dots + p) - (1^2 + 2^2 + \dots + 9^2) \ge 1$
$\Rightarrow \frac{p(p+1)}{2} - \frac{9(10)(19)}{6} \ge 1$
$\Rightarrow p(p + 1) \ge 572$
$\Rightarrow$ Least natural values of $p$ is $24$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Let $f : (0, \infty) \to \mathbf{R}$ be a twice differentiable function. If for some $a \neq 0$, $\int_{0}^{1} f(\lambda x) d\lambda = a f(x)$, $f(1) = 1$ and $f(16) = \frac{1}{8}$, then $16 - f'\left(\frac{1}{16}\right)$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Given, $\int_{0}^{1} f(\lambda x) d\lambda = a f(x)$ ...(1)
Let $\lambda x = u$
$d\lambda = \frac{1}{x} du$
$\therefore$ From (1) $\frac{1}{x} \int_{0}^{x} f(u) du = a f(x)$
$\Rightarrow \int_{0}^{x} f(u) du = a x f(x)$
Differentiate both sides
$f(x) = a(x f'(x) + f(x))$
$\Rightarrow f(x) = a x f'(x) + a f(x)$
$\Rightarrow (1 - a) f(x) = a x f'(x)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)} = \frac{(1 - a)}{a} \cdot \frac{1}{x}$
Integrate both side w.r.t. $(x)$
$\Rightarrow \int \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)} dx = \frac{(1 - a)}{a} \int \frac{1}{x} dx$
$\Rightarrow \ln f(x) = \left(\frac{1 - a}{a}\right) \ln x + c$
Now at $x = 1$, $f(1) = 1$
$\Rightarrow c = 0$
Also given $f(16) = \frac{1}{8}$
$\therefore \frac{1}{8} = (16)^{\frac{1-a}{a}}$
$\Rightarrow 2^{-3} = 2^{\frac{4-4a}{a}}$
$\Rightarrow -3 = \frac{4 - 4a}{a}$
$\Rightarrow -3a = 4 - 4a$
$\Rightarrow a = 4$
$\therefore f(x) = x^{-3/4}$
$f'(x) = -\frac{3}{4} x^{-7/4}$
Put $x = \frac{1}{16}$
$f'\left(\frac{1}{16}\right) = -\frac{3}{4} \left(\frac{1}{16}\right)^{-7/4} = -\frac{3}{4} \cdot 2^7 = -96$
$\therefore 16 - f'\left(\frac{1}{16}\right) \Rightarrow 16 - (-96) = 112$

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Choke coil is simply a coil having a large inductance but a small resistance. Choke coils are used with fluorescent mercury-tube fittings. If household electric power is directly connected to a mercury tube, the tube will be damaged.
Reason (R) : By using the choke coil, the voltage across the tube is reduced by a factor $\left( R / \sqrt{R^2 + \omega^2 L^2} \right)$, where $\omega$ is frequency of the supply across resistor $R$ and inductor $L$. If the choke coil were not used, the voltage across the resistor would be the same as the applied voltage.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: (1) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(2) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
$I = \frac{V}{\sqrt{R^2 + \omega^2 L^2}}$
$V_R = \frac{R}{\sqrt{R^2 + \omega^2 L^2}} V$

questions.text: If $\lambda$ and $K$ are de Broglie wavelength and kinetic energy, respectively, of a particle with constant mass. The correct graphical representation for the particle will be
questions.solution:
$\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$
$\lambda^2 = \frac{h^2}{2mK}$
$\frac{1}{K} = \left(\frac{2m}{h^2}\right) \lambda^2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Consider $I_1$ and $I_2$ are the currents flowing simultaneously in two nearby coils 1 & 2, respectively. If $L_1 =$ self inductance of coil 1, $M_{12} =$ mutual inductance of coil 1 with respect to coil 2, then the value of induced emf in coil 1 will be
questions.solution: Magnitude of induced emf due to self inductance $= \frac{L dI_1}{dt}$. Magnitude of induced emf due to mutual inductance $= \frac{M dI_2}{dt}$. Thus, $\varepsilon_1 = -L_1 \frac{dI_1}{dt} - M_{12} \frac{dI_2}{dt}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: An electric dipole of mass $m$, charge $q$, and length $l$ is placed in a uniform electric field $\vec{E} = E_0\hat{i}$. When the dipole is rotated slightly from its equilibrium position and released, the time period of its oscillations will be :
questions.solution: $\tau = PE_0 \sin\theta$. If $\theta$ is small, $\tau = -(PE_0)\theta$. $I = m\left(\frac{l}{2}\right)^2 \cdot 2 = \frac{ml^2}{2}$. $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{ml^2}{2 \cdot PE_0}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{ml^2}{2 \cdot qlE_0}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{ml}{2qE_0}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: As shown below, bob $A$ of a pendulum having massless string of length '$R$' is released from $60^\circ$ to the vertical. It hits another bob $B$ of half the mass that is at rest on a frictionless table in the center. Assuming elastic collision, the magnitude of the velocity of bob $A$ after the collision will be (take $g$ as acceleration due to gravity.)
questions.solution: Velocity of $A$ before collision $= \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2g \times \frac{R}{2}} = \sqrt{Rg}$. COM: $mu = \frac{m}{2}v_1 + mv_2 \Rightarrow 2u = v_1 + 2v_2$. Also $e = 1 \Rightarrow u = v_1 - v_2 \Rightarrow u = 3v_2 \Rightarrow v_2 = \frac{u}{3} = \frac{1}{3}\sqrt{Rg}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Electric field inside (distance $r > 0$ from center) of a uniformly charged spherical shell with surface charge density $\sigma$, and radius $R$. (B) Electric field at distance $r > 0$ from a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet with surface charge density $\sigma$. (C) Electric field outside (distance $r > 0$ from center) of a uniformly charged spherical shell with surface charge density $\sigma$, and radius $R$. (D) Electric field between 2 oppositely charged infinite plane parallel sheets with uniform surface charge density $\sigma$. List-II: (I) $\sigma / \varepsilon_0$ (II) $\sigma / 2\varepsilon_0$ (III) $0$ (IV) $\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0 r^2}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Inside uniformly charged spherical shell, $E = 0 \Rightarrow A \rightarrow III$. For uniformly charged infinite plate, $E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0} \Rightarrow B \rightarrow II$. Outside of spherical shell, $E = \frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2} = \frac{\sigma R^2}{\varepsilon_0 r^2}$. None of the option is matching for C. Between two plates $E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0} \Rightarrow D \rightarrow I$. None of the option is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The fractional compression $\left(\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right)$ of water at the depth of $2.5\text{ km}$ below the sea level is ______ %. Given, the Bulk modulus of water $= 2 \times 10^9\text{ Nm}^{-2}$, density of water $= 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}$, acceleration due to gravity $= g = 10\text{ ms}^{-2}$.
questions.solution: $B = \frac{\Delta P}{-\left(\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right)} \Rightarrow -\left(\frac{\Delta V}{V}\right) = \frac{\Delta P}{B} = \frac{\rho g h}{B} = \frac{10^3 \times 10 \times 2.5 \times 10^3}{2 \times 10^9} = 1.25\%$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $a_0$ is denoted as the Bohr radius of hydrogen atom, then what is the de-Broglie wavelength $(\lambda)$ of the electron present in the second orbit of hydrogen atom? [$n$ : any integer]
questions.solution:
$r_n = \frac{a_0 n^2}{z}$
Also, $2\pi r_n = n\lambda$
Where $\lambda$ is de-Broglie wavelength
$\frac{2\pi a_0 n^2}{z} = n\lambda$
For second orbit of H-atom
$\lambda = \frac{8\pi a_0}{n}$

(A) $[\text{MnBr}_4]^{2-}$
(B) $[\text{FeF}_6]^{3-}$
(C) $[\text{Co(C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}$
(D) $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$

(I) $d^2sp^3$ & diamagnetic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:

$[\text{Co(C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-} : \text{Co}^{3+}, \text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ is a SFL $\Rightarrow d^6$, so it is $d^2sp^3$ and diamagnetic.
$[\text{Ni(CO)}_4] : \text{CO}$ is a SFL $\Rightarrow d^{10}$, it is $sp^3$ and diamagnetic.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
The correct increasing order of stability of the complexes based on $\Delta_0$ value is:
I. $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$
II. $[\text{Co(CN)}_6]^{4-}$
III. $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$
IV. $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}$
questions.solution:
Neglecting pairing energy:
I. $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-} \Rightarrow \text{Mn}^{3+}, t_{2g}^4, \text{CFSE} = -0.4 \times 4 \Delta_0 = -1.6\Delta_0$
II. $[\text{Co(CN)}_6]^{4-} \Rightarrow \text{Co}^{2+}, t_{2g}^6 e_g^1, \text{CFSE} = -0.4 \times 6 + 0.6 \times 1 = -1.8\Delta_0$
III. $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-} \Rightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+}, t_{2g}^6 e_g^0, \text{CFSE} = -0.4 \times 6 = -2.4\Delta_0$
IV. $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-} \Rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+}, t_{2g}^5 e_g^0, \text{CFSE} = -0.4 \times 5 = -2\Delta_0$
Order of stability III > IV > II > I
